validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki harvest for this scope returned HTTP 403 for every row (wiki_citations.json confirms P4020 = ok:false/403), so there was no existing cited source to re-verify; I also tried WebFetch on the row's own wiki URL directly and got the same 403 (Cloudflare), so no leads could be pulled from GEM's page either -- this is a clean-slate research task, not a re-verification. Went straight to open-web/Pakistani-utility research per scope guidance. Found SSGC's own official 'Gas Transmission Capacities Utilization as on June 30, 2018' page (ssgc.com.pk/web/?page_id=5597, verified OK via url_verifier: 200 + all of 'Bajara-Karachi Loopline', 'Dadu-Malir-Karachi', '400', 'IRBP' present). That page lists the Indus Right Bank Pipeline (IRBP) System as comprising exactly two segments: '20"/18" dia. x250 Km IRBP Pipeline Dadu-Malir-Karachi' (400 mmscfd) -- matching GEM's P4019 -- and '24" dia. x200 Km Bajara-Karachi Loopline' (240 mmscfd) -- matching GEM's P4020 EXACTLY on name, length (200 km), diameter (24 in) and capacity (240 MMcf/d). This is a direct statement from the pipeline's own owner/operator (SSGC), independent of GEM, and it resolves my initial existence/duplicate suspicion cleanly: P4020 is real, is correctly a SEPARATE row from P4019 (SSGC itself treats them as two distinct segments of one IRBP system, i.e. a genuine mainline+loopline pair, not a double-count), and every spec value on the sheet is correct as recorded. I also pulled a Petroleum Division/PPIS 2025 Investment Brochure network map (ppisonline.com/Brochure/Investment%20Brochure%202025.pdf -- a scanned/image map; pdftotext -layout extraction) which appeared to show an overlapping label reading '24"X64 KM BAJARA-KARCHAT ... LOOPLINE (YEAR 2006)', i.e. a much shorter (64 km) segment tied to a place called 'Karchat' (a real, distinct town in Thano Bula Khan tehsil, Jamshoro District -- confirmed via web search -- NOT Karachi city) rather than 'Karachi'. This briefly raised an attribution flag (mistranscribed endpoint). However, since SSGC's own official page independently and exactly matches GEM's name/length/diameter/capacity to the digit, I now treat the PPIS map reading as an unreliable OCR/label-association artifact of a jumbled scanned map (text-extraction order on dense map graphics frequently interleaves unrelated overlapping labels) rather than evidence against GEM's data, or possibly a reference to a different, smaller, unrelated spur near the Bhit gas field's 'Bajara' tie-in point that predates or feeds into the larger loopline SSGC now reports. I did not cite the PPIS map. Searched extensively (OGRA tariff/ERR determinations, SNGPL/SSGC network maps, PPIS 2023 brochure [404], Scribd SSGC decks, academic/NGO gas-sector reports) for a second independent source with matching segment-level detail and did not find one, so tier is medium (one strong, authoritative, operator-published source) rather than high. Classification (transmission) is correct: SSGC's page places this pipeline within its high-pressure transmission network table alongside the other named trunk/loop systems (IRBP, Indus Left Bank Pipeline, Quetta Pipeline System, RLNG-2), not among distribution or gathering lines. Owner (Sui Southern Gas Co, 100%) is confirmed by the same source, since it is literally SSGC's own published capacity-utilization table for its own transmission assets. One residual minor caveat, not escalated to a concern: the pipeline's own name implies its start point is 'Bajara' (a locality I could not independently pin to a specific village/coordinate), while GEM records StartLocation as 'Dadu' -- plausible if Bajara sits within Dadu district on the same IRBP corridor as P4019, but I could not independently confirm the micro-location beyond SSGC's own naming convention.
